facts.statement: The holotype of Tsaagan was discovered in 1996 and initially misidentified as a Velociraptor.
facts.quote: The holotype of Tsaagan was discovered in 1996 and first identified as a specimen of Velociraptor.

facts.statement: A CAT-scan performed in May 1998 revealed that the specimen represented a new genus.
facts.quote: After a CAT-scan in May 1998 it was concluded that it represented a new genus.

facts.statement: The type species was formally named and described in December 2006 by Mark Norell, James Clark, Alan Turner, Peter Makovicky, Rinchen Barsbold, and Timothy Rowe.
facts.quote: In December 2006 its type species was named and described by Mark Norell, James Clark, Alan Turner, Peter Makovicky, Rinchen Barsbold and Timothy Rowe.

facts.statement: The holotype was found near Xanadu in Ömnögovi Province within the Djadokhta Formation, dating to the Campanian stage about 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, IGM 100/1015, was found near Xanadu in Ömnögovi Province in layers of the Djadokhta Formation dating to the Campanian, about 75 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a well-preserved skull, ten neck vertebrae, and a damaged left shoulder girdle.
facts.quote: It consists of a well-preserved skull and series of ten neck vertebrae as well as a damaged left shoulder girdle.

facts.statement: The holotype is the only known specimen of Tsaagan and belonged to an adult individual.
facts.quote: It is the only specimen found of Tsaagan and belonged to an adult individual.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Tsaagan's length at 2 meters and its weight at 15 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 2 m, its weight at 15 kg.

facts.statement: Tsaagan is classified as a member of the group Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Tsaagan is a member of the group Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: An original cladistic analysis by Norell et al. indicated that Tsaagan was a member of the subfamily Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis by Norell et al. originally indicated it was more precisely a member of the Velociraptorinae.

facts.statement: Later analyses suggested Tsaagan was closely related to Linheraptor, leading some researchers to argue that Linheraptor exquisitus is a junior synonym of Tsaagan mangas.
facts.quote: In 2010 an analysis showed it was closely related to Linheraptor; subsequently Senter (2011) and Turner, Makovicky and Norell (2012) argued that Linheraptor exquisitus is in fact a junior synonym of Tsaagan mangas.

facts.statement: Xu, Pittman et al. (2015) reject the synonymy of Linheraptor exquisitus with Tsaagan mangas, citing new and existing anatomical details.
facts.quote: Xu, Pittman et al. (2015) reject this synonymy by responding to the counterarguments proposed using new and existing details of Linheraptor's anatomy.

facts.statement: Tsaagan lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Tsaagan represents the only known dromaeosaurid remains, aside from isolated teeth, from the Ukhaa Tolgod region, although Velociraptor is also known from the Djadokhta Formation.
facts.quote: Tsaagan representa los únicos restos de dromeosáuridos, aparte de dientes aislados, conocidos de la región de Ukhaa Tolgod, aunque se conoce otro dromeosáurido, Velociraptor, de la misma Formación Djadokhta.

facts.statement: Animals that may have shared Tsaagan's habitat include Protoceratops, Shuvuuia, the small mammal Zalambdalestes, the multituberculate mammal Kryptobaatar, various lizards, and undescribed troodontid and dromaeosaurid species.
facts.quote: Los animales que pueden haber compartido el mismo hábitat con Tsaagan incluyen Protoceratops, Shuvuuia , el pequeño mamífero Zalambdalestes, el mamífero multituberculado Kryptobaatar, así como varias lagartijas y un trodóntido y un dromeosáurido sin describir.

facts.statement: The time range for Tsaagan is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The name Tsaagan mangas is derived from the Mongolian words for "white monster," though it contains an accidental misspelling of the word for white.
rejected.quote: The species name, Tsaagan mangas, should be read as a whole with the generic name qualifying the specific epithet, and is derived from the Mongolian words for "white monster" (цагаан мангас), although with an accidental misspelling of the word Tsagaan.

rejected.statement: Unique derived traits include long paroccipital processes and basipterygoids at the back of the skull and a jugal bone touching the squamosal.
rejected.quote: unique derived traits, autapomorphies, include long paroccipital processes and basipterygoids at the back of the skull and a jugal touching the squamosal.
